person: Tom Whitcomb is the administrator of a three-clinician primary care clinic that bills Original Medicare. He came from restaurant management and learns billing by asking his biller, Dana, who works three days a week and is out today. It is the end of October and the owners keep asking why Medicare collections are down. He suspects some patients were billed for denied lab lines they should not have been, and some who paid should get money back. He wants a list of numbers he can defend to the owners, in plain words.
stated_up_front: Dana's out today and I need to go through this month's denied Medicare lab lines: who we can actually bill and who we owe money back. Explain it to me like I'm the guy who has to tell the doctors, and please don't send anything to patients or refund anyone without checking with me.

facts.truth: Three clinicians (two physicians and one nurse practitioner); Original Medicare is billed through Novabridge.
October 2026 denials, with remittances dated in October.

facts.about: Number of denied Medicare lab lines this month
facts.truth: Dana's check list shows 11 denied lines, mostly lab tests such as vitamin D, A1c and lipid panels.
Front desk has every Medicare patient sign an ABN at check-in, and Tom believes it just says 'labs may not be covered' with no specific reason.

facts.about: Patients who have already paid at the desk
facts.truth: Four patients paid for lab lines at the desk or online, roughly $18 to $62 each, about $165 in total, and he doesn't know which ones are valid.
One patient had a second blood draw in the same visit, and Medicare denied it. The patient has an ABN for it and Tom assumes that means the patient owes it.
Tom recalls the front desk may have kept using the old printed ABN forms from a box in the supply closet into the late summer.
Dana's policy is that no Medicare patient statement goes out until she or Tom has looked at the line. Some statements are on hold in Chartmend PM.
At least one refund was already sent in September to a patient who complained, and Tom isn't sure which one.
He will take the totals (billable to patients, refund owed, clinic absorbs) to the owners at the Monday meeting.

unknowns: Whether a given ABN is on the current form version, or when the old form stopped being accepted
What the group and reason codes on the Novabridge remittance mean (GA, GZ, CO, PR and so on)
Whether a second blood draw denial is a limit Medicare sets on units per day and so can never be billed to the patient
Which of this month's patients were already refunded in September
